description: Conformance fixture register. Every fixture file in this directory is listed here exactly once; the Dart validator, the watchOS suite, and the Wear OS suite walk this manifest rather than a hardcoded list. Every reconciliation fixture is replayed by the conformance test and must converge on its `expected` state; each entry under `scenarios` records the property the fixture pins, and the plan scenario it belongs to where there is one (`scenario` is null for fixtures that pin a protocol rule rather than a plan scenario).

valid.note: An empty Foods I Eat list is a frame like any other: `foods` and `categories` are both empty, and the wrist applies it, emptying the list it holds.
The family's shape: `ex-bench` carries only the weight axis — a full-precision Epley estimate, never rounded (D-10) — and `ex-push-up` only the reps axis, the bodyweight set's rep best.
An empty frame is a frame: `bests: []` tells the wrist the phone knows of no history, so every first set is a PR.
One entry may carry both axes: `ex-bench` holds a weighted best and a bodyweight rep best, so "at least one axis" is a floor, not an exclusive-or.
The family's shape: the phone's day, its own glass count, and the wrist taps that count already includes, in the order the phone applied them (plan 94 D-6).
A day with no water is a frame like any other: `glasses: 0` and an empty `appliedTapIds` tell the wrist to count from 0.
Two glass taps under the day's nutrition id: a `water_glass` entry names no slot and no exercise, and carries `glassChange` as a closed string, never a signed number (plan 94 D-2).
F-6(b): pausedMs equal to its window is a real wire value (A-30 caps a round's pause at the window), so equality must be accepted, not just below it.
A set's loadKg may be negative down to -200 kg (a band or partner assist); `evt-assist-1` carries -20 and `evt-assist-2` the floor -200.
The phone's snapshot carries an assisted set verbatim: `entry-slot-bench-0` is -20 kg and `entry-slot-bench-1` the floor -200 kg.
A routine target may be negative too: `eff-bench` targets -20 kg and `eff-goblet-squat` the floor -200 kg.
A rest is a window between two instants: `rest-a1` is the 70 s `rest` that follows the set `entry-a1`, named by `afterEntryId` and carrying no planned length.

A slot MAY carry the phone's period length: `sx-soccer` is a round slot at 2400 s and `sx-soccer-plain` the same slot with the field omitted. `sx-marathon` carries 86400 s — the schema declares `minimum: 1` and no maximum, so this slot is the top of the range the walker accepts (S-1412).

A `set` slot MAY carry the phone's planned sets: `sx-bench` holds three rows in set order — 10 reps at 40 kg twice, then 8 reps at 42.5 kg — and holds no entries, so all three rows are still to come. A slot with no set rows, a non-set slot, or an older phone omits the key.
The routine's round effort keeps the phone's target: `eff-soccer-half` carries `durationMs: 600000` (600 s) while `eff-soccer-extra` has no length target and `eff-plank` is a `timed` effort.

A phone with exercises and no routine still sends: `routines` is empty and `fallbackExercises` carries every exercise the phone offers the wrist — a set, a hold, and a round with its own period length.
An empty catalog is valid: the phone has no routines and nothing extra to offer, so `routines` and `fallbackExercises` are both empty. The fallback list is not required to hold anything.
The first batch of a two-batch list: `catalogVersion` `v1-4-a1b2c3d4`, `batchIndex` 0 of `batchCount` 2, `totalCount` 4, carrying two exercises — a set and a round with its own period length.
A list that fits in one batch: `batchCount` 1, `batchIndex` 0, `totalCount` 3, three exercises.
A distance exercise MAY name its Health kind: `ex-ride` carries `healthActivity: "cycling"` while `ex-bench`, a lifting exercise, carries no such key.
A routine effort and the fallback list MAY name the Health kind too: `ef-ride` and the `ex-ride` fallback both carry `healthActivity: "cycling"`.
A session slot MAY name the Health kind: `sx-hike` carries `healthActivity: "hiking"` with `capabilities` `["time", "distance"]`.
The phone's session MAY carry its Focus to the wrist: `s-2026-07-13-1` carries `modality: "isometric_stretching"`, a non-empty string, phone to watch only (plan 125d).
A cardio session's snapshot names `modality: "cardio_endurance"` with one distance exercise and no entries yet: the key is optional and the session's own (plan 125d).
A routine MAY carry the phone's Focus Modality: `routine-isometric-a` names `focusModality: "isometric_stretching"`, present only when the routine has a Focus and never empty (plan 125a).

invalid.note: A batch is one of `batchCount` slices, so its 0-based `batchIndex` is always below `batchCount`: index 2 of 2 names a slice the list does not have.
`totalCount` is the whole list's size, so it cannot be smaller than the exercises one batch already carries: 1 total against two exercises is impossible.
The batches must be able to carry the whole list: one batch of at most 100 cannot hold 101 exercises.
An exercise appears once in the list, so the same `exerciseId` twice in one batch is a defect.
Every batch carries at least one exercise: a list that needs no batches carries no `exercises_down` at all.
A batch names the version of the whole list it belongs to; without `catalogVersion` the wrist cannot tell which list it is assembling.

The only fixture that carries a remaining-time field, on purpose: the field is the defect. Every fixture that represents timer state must be free of one — see test/sync_protocol_fixtures_test.dart (S-003).

invalid.expectedReasonContains: a rest has no planned length
invalid.note: A rest is a count-up, so a planned length on a rest timer is the defect (D-164, docs/global_conventions.md rest rule). Every other timer kind keeps its plannedDurationMs — valid/timer_state.json carries the rest without one.

invalid.expectedReasonContains: a rest has no planned length
invalid.note: The refusal is not timer_state-only: a snapshot carrying a rest plan is refused too (D-164, D-169). Without this fixture the snapshot branch's clause is unreachable, which is exactly the gap it pins.

invalid.expectedReasonContains: steps is carried only by timed entries
avgHeartRateBpm is carried only by timed, round, hold, session_end entries
avgHeartRateBpm must not exceed maxHeartRateBpm, but does on e-bad-hr-order
pausedMs is carried only by round entries
setBlockHeartRates is carried only by session_end entries
does not match the required pattern
the slot it logged it in; missing on e-snap-noslot
pausedMs must not exceed the time between startedAt and endedAt
avgHeartRateBpm must not exceed maxHeartRateBpm, but does on end-s-cap-bad set block sx-bench/ex-bench
a set block may appear once per sessionExerciseId and exerciseId pair
rating is carried only by effort_rating entries
status is carried only by session_end entries
followed is carried only by session_end entries
modality is carried only by session_end entries

invalid.note: F-6(a): capture-field placement is unguarded on a snapshot's own entries unless a snapshot fixture exercises it too — the observations_up fixture above does not reach that code path.
F-10: a JSON `3200.0` is a double. Dart's `value is int` refuses it, and the Swift validator must too, or the two disagree on the same bytes (review N6 pins the wording as well).

invalid.expectedReasonContains: distanceSource is carried only by timed entries

invalid.note: The floor is shared by every loadKg the protocol defines; -240 kg is below it and MUST be refused, not clamped.
A rest must name the set it follows: the eighth event shape requires afterEntryId.
A rest is a count-up: the shared entry shape carries no plannedDurationMs, so the event is refused.
A rest of no length cannot travel: endedAt is not after startedAt, so the window rule refuses it.
A round length of 0 is not a length: the schema's minimum is 1.
A negative round length is below the schema's minimum of 1.
The length is whole seconds: 12.5 is a number, not an integer.
The length is a number, never a string: `"2400"` is refused as the wrong type.
A planned row of 0 reps is not a row the wrist can dial in: `reps` declares `minimum: 1`, and a row with fewer than 1 rep is a skipped row the phone omits rather than sends.
A planned row is a closed object: its position in the array IS the set number, so a `setNumber` key is a field the schema does not define and the snapshot is refused.
The Focus is never empty: `modality: ""` trips the key's `minLength`; the wrist applies a modality key only when it has one.
The Focus is a string: `modality: 7` is refused whole at `$.payload.modality`.
The Focus is never null: a session with none OMITS the key, so `modality: null` is a type refusal, not a none.
The Focus is one key, not a list: `modality: ["sports"]` is refused whole.
A snapshot carries the SESSION's key: the routine's `focusModality` name is a field the snapshot schema does not define, so the frame is refused.
The session's Focus rides the payload, never an entry: `e-1`, a `set` entry, carrying `modality` is refused by the capture-field gate.
`healthActivity` is a closed enum: `"swimming"` is not one of the five kinds the phone can name, so the batch is refused.

invalid.expectedReasonContains: entry carries neither e1rmKg nor repsBest
invalid.note: An entry that states neither number says nothing about the exercise, so the frame is refused. The dialect has no `anyOf`, so the floor is a semantic rule (D-14).
A zero estimate is not a best: the schema's `minimum` admits 0 (the dialect has no `exclusiveMinimum`), so the bound above it is a semantic rule (D-14).
A rep count is whole: `repsBest` declares `type: integer`, so 12.5 is refused rather than rounded.

invalid.expectedReasonContains: the same exerciseId appears twice: ex-bench
invalid.note: One frame states an exercise's best once: two entries for one `exerciseId` would leave the wrist deciding which is current (D-14).

invalid.expectedReasonContains: field "unit" is not defined by the schema
invalid.note: The payload is closed: `unit` is a field the schema does not define, and the frame is refused rather than read for the parts it does have.
`bests_down` is reference data the phone owns, so its origin is `phone` and a wrist-originated copy is refused (D-2).
The frame is ONE message capped at 300 entries (D-9): 301 is refused by `maxItems`, and the phone's own builder neither batches nor exceeds the cap.

invalid.expectedReasonContains: field "volumeMl" is not defined by the schema
invalid.note: The payload is closed: the count travels as glasses, never as a volume, and an unknown field refuses the frame.
A glass count is never negative: the phone clamps its volume at 0.
`glasses` is the phone's whole-glass count (volume divided by the glass, rounded down), so a fraction is refused rather than rounded.

invalid.expectedReasonContains: does not match the required pattern
invalid.note: `day` is a zero-padded `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar date, compared as a string with the wrist's own date; a locale-formatted date is refused.

invalid.expectedReasonContains: the same tap id appears twice: w-1
invalid.note: The phone applies a tap once, so its id is listed once; a repeated id is a sender defect (plan 94 D-10).
The phone owns the day's water, so the count's origin is `phone` and a wrist-originated copy is refused.
The phone records at most 500 wrist taps a day, so a frame never lists more: 501 is refused by `maxItems`.
A glass tap without its direction says nothing the phone can apply, so the message is refused.
`glassChange` is a closed enum: a tap is one glass added or removed, nothing else.

invalid.expectedReasonContains: field "volumeMl" is not defined by the schema
invalid.note: A tap is a one-glass change, never an amount: a volume on the event is a field the schema does not define, and the whole message is refused.

invalid.expectedReasonContains: glassChange is carried only by water_glass entries
invalid.note: `glassChange` belongs to a glass tap; on a set it is a sender defect (plan 94 D-10).
A routine's Focus Modality is a key when it is named at all: an empty string is no modality and is refused by `minLength`.
`focusModality` is a string, never a number: 7 is refused as the wrong type.

scenarios.property: replaying the stream twice equals applying it once
removing the current exercise advances to the next valid one
the same exercise in two slots is two addresses
every structure-change kind applies in order
a second snapshot merges entries and replaces structure and timers
a null timer clears; an unnamed timer survives
lifecycle states apply in order and out-of-range positions clamp
a session reported started is live again
a slot id can be introduced only once
version mismatch rejects and answers with a snapshot
a snapshot for another session replaces the held one, entries included
a snapshot adds the entries the phone logged, once each, and replaces structure
a re-stated band-assisted set is neither duplicated nor zeroed
